title: Common tests: t-test, chi-square, ANOVA and non-parametric tests

videos.script: Lessons thirteen to fifteen built one test, on one mean, against one fixed value. Real questions come in more shapes than that. {{shapes}} Are deliveries to Centro faster than deliveries to Cambuí? Two groups. {{two}} Did the same ten couriers get faster after a training course? The same people measured twice. {{paired}} Did the new checkout page sell to more visitors than the old one? Counts of yes and no, in two groups. {{counts}} Do the four neighbourhoods differ in delivery time? Four groups at once. {{four}} Each shape has its own test, and choosing among them takes two questions. What kind of outcome is it, a number or a category? And how many groups are being compared? {{questions}} The logic never changes. A null hypothesis of no difference, a statistic measuring signal against noise, and a p-value. Only the arithmetic changes. {{logic}} This lesson runs each test on Horta's data. It shows the one mistake that turns a significant result into a non-significant one, and gives a rank-based alternative for every test of means. {{ranks}}
